rows.figure: 57 deaths: vessel disaster 21, onboard injury 14, fall overboard 12, onshore 7, diving 3
rows.scope: Work-related traumatic-injury deaths of commercial fishermen in NIOSH's Alaska region, 2015-2019, Commercial Fishing Incident Database (CFID), by the source's own incident types: vessel disaster 21 (37%), onboard injury 14 (25%), fall overboard 12 (21%), onshore injury 7 (12%), diving 3 (5%). Drowning is named as the cause for the 12 falls overboard, all 7 onshore deaths (falls from docks) and 2 of 3 diving deaths; the cause of death of the 21 vessel-disaster victims is not stated. Onboard deaths include 7 overdoses, 4 suicides, 1 homicide. Five-year period, not one year; no ICD codes printed.
rows.source: NIOSH, Commercial Fishing Fatality Summary: Alaska Region, 2015-2019, DHHS (NIOSH) Publication No. 2025-112, Figure 2 and the Falls Overboard, Onshore and Diving sections
rows.do_not_add_to: CFID incident-type counts, not vital statistics: do not add to CDC W65-W74 counts, us-cdc-4500, us-cdc-4345, us-total-2022, uscg-boating-2024 or us-location-boating-2024 (recreational vessels), or to WHO/IHME. A subset of us-fishing-deaths-2000-2019-niosh (Alaska 236) and overlapping us-fishing-drowning-share-2010-2014: never added to either. Not combined with the BLS CFOI occupation count (different case-finding). Do not turn the named drownings into a W65-W74 share: the ICD code of each death is not published.
rows.note: Figure 2 labels came out of the PDF as 17, 12, 14, 7, 3, 4; 17 and 4 are most likely decked-vessel and skiff vessel disasters (the Alaska reports split them), which the text gives as 21 together. A reviewer should confirm Figure 2 by eye. Earlier Alaska summaries cover 2000-2009 and 2010-2014. Footnote 1 names CFID as the data source.

rows.figure: 878 deaths: vessel disasters 414, falls overboard 266, onboard 122, diving or onshore 76
rows.scope: Work-related traumatic-injury deaths of commercial fishermen, United States, 2000-2019, NIOSH Commercial Fishing Incident Database, by incident type: after a vessel disaster 414 (47%), falls overboard 266 (30%), injuries onboard 122 (14%), diving or onshore 76 (9%); by region East Coast 288, Alaska 236, Gulf of Mexico 201, West Coast 141, Hawaii/Pacific 12. A twenty-year total averaging over 43 a year; no single-year counts, no cause of death and no ICD codes on the page.
rows.source: NIOSH, Commercial Fishing Safety in the United States (regional summaries: national overview), web page dated 15 January 2025
rows.do_not_add_to: A period total: never divided into years or added to any annual row. Contains us-fishing-alaska-incident-types-2015-2019 and the periods of us-fishing-drowning-share-2000-2009 and us-fishing-drowning-share-2010-2014: never added to them. Not vital statistics: do not add to CDC W65-W74 counts, us-cdc-4500, us-cdc-4345, us-total-2022, the USCG recreational-boating rows or WHO/IHME; not combined with the BLS CFOI occupation count.
rows.note: The only year-specific statement on the page is a rate: in 2019 commercial fishermen died at work at over 40 times the all-worker rate (attributed to BLS). The database's sources (Coast Guard reports, law enforcement, media, death certificates and state surveillance programmes) are stated in Lucas & Case 2018 and Lincoln & Lucas 2010, not on this page.

rows.figure: 139 of 188 deaths (75%) with drowning as the reported cause
rows.scope: Deaths of commercial fishermen, United States, 2010-2014, NIOSH Commercial Fishing Incident Database (188 deaths: vessel disasters 80, falls overboard 57, onboard injuries 31, diving 14, onshore 6; East Coast 60, Gulf of Mexico 49, Alaska 45, West Coast 30, Hawaii 4), for which drowning was the reported cause of death: 139 (75%). The paper says causes of death are coded in ICD-10 from death certificates or investigative reports but prints no codes, so how many of the 139 sit in W65-W74 rather than V90/V92 is not published.
rows.source: Lucas and Case (2018), Work-related mortality in the US fishing industry during 2000-2014: new findings based on improved workforce exposure estimates, Am J Ind Med 61(1):21-31, author manuscript on CDC Stacks, Results p. 4, Case Definition p. 2, Table III
rows.do_not_add_to: A cause-of-death count within one five-year CFID period: do not add to us-fishing-drowning-share-2000-2009 (other years), to us-fishing-deaths-2000-2019-niosh or us-fishing-alaska-incident-types-2015-2019 (which contain or overlap it), to CDC W65-W74 counts, us-cdc-4500, us-cdc-4345, us-total-2022 or WHO/IHME. 'Drowning' is the reported cause, not an ICD code group: never read as a W65-W74 count.
rows.note: The other 49 deaths are not itemised by cause in the text read; onboard causes 2010-2014 include gear entanglement 7, poisoning 6 (unintentional drug overdoses) and struck by gear 5. Four Hawaii deaths were drownings after falls overboard.

rows.scope: Share of the 504 deaths of commercial fishermen in the United States, 2000-2009 (NIOSH CFID: vessel disasters 261, falls overboard 155, onboard injuries 51, diving 19, onshore 18) whose cause of death was drowning: 86%. No count of drownings is printed. Causes of death coded in ICD-10 from death certificates or investigative reports (Methods); codes not printed.
rows.source: Lincoln and Lucas (2010), Occupational fatalities in the United States commercial fishing industry, 2000-2009, Journal of Agromedicine 15:343-350, CDC Stacks copy, Results p. 346 and Methods p. 345
rows.do_not_add_to: A share for one period: never averaged with us-fishing-drowning-share-2010-2014 (75%) or applied to any other period, region or country's fisher count; not a W65-W74 share. The 504 deaths sit inside us-fishing-deaths-2000-2019-niosh (878) and must not be added to it, nor to CDC counts or WHO/IHME.
rows.note: The same 504 deaths and incident-type split appear in MMWR 59(27):842-845 (16 July 2010), which does not use the word drowning but states that CFID causes of death come from death certificates or investigative reports and are coded in ICD-10 (cited in evidence).

rows.figure: 66 of 70 deaths (94.3%) drowning, presumed drowning or drowning due to hypothermia
rows.scope: Commercial fishing deaths in Alaska, 1991-1992 (35 in each year), identified by NIOSH from Coast Guard data, survivor interviews and death certificates, with ICD-9 external-cause codes 830, 831, 832, 834, 836, 838 and 910 listed as the case-finding codes: 66 drownings (51 after capsized, sunk or missing vessels, 15 after person-overboard events; 21 confirmed with body recovered, 45 presumed), 3 crushed during crabbing, 1 suicide. The report does not say how many deaths carried each code.
rows.source: CDC, MMWR 42(18):350, 14 May 1993, Commercial Fishing Fatalities - Alaska, 1991-1992, Methods and Results
rows.do_not_add_to: Historical (ICD-9 era) and Alaska only: not added to any NIOSH CFID period (which starts in 2000), to the BLS CFOI count, to CDC or Alaska vital-statistics drowning counts, or to WHO/IHME. The 94.3% is not applied to other years or regions. The code list shows that both water-transport and accidental-drowning codes were used to find fisher deaths; it gives no per-code count and no W65-W74 equivalent share.
rows.note: Recorded because it is the only source found that prints the external-cause codes used to find fisher deaths. The report does not map ICD-9 codes to ICD-10; a reviewer should check the correspondence before using them.

rows.scope: Fatal occupational injuries of workers in the occupation 'Fishing and hunting workers', United States, calendar 2024, BLS Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries (data for all years revised and final). Earlier years in the same table: 2020 = 42, 2021 = 23, 2022 = 16, 2023 = 19. Occupation of the decedent, not fishing-industry activity as in NIOSH CFID; all events. The table gives no split by event (water-vehicle incident versus drowning), and CFOI uses OIICS event codes, not ICD.
rows.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries, 2024 release, Table 3: Fatal occupational injuries for selected occupations, 2020-24
rows.do_not_add_to: A different case definition from NIOSH CFID (decedent's occupation versus fishing-industry activity): never added to or reconciled with us-fishing-deaths-2000-2019-niosh or us-fishing-alaska-incident-types-2015-2019. Not vital statistics: do not add to CDC W65-W74 counts, us-cdc-4500, us-cdc-4345, us-total-2022, the USCG rows or WHO/IHME. Includes non-drowning deaths and gives no drowning share.
rows.note: The occupation-by-event table (A-5) is published as a spreadsheet and was not read; it would split the 24 into transportation (water-vehicle) incidents and other events.

rows.figure: 63 of 216 watercraft-related drowning deaths (29%) had W65-74 as underlying cause
rows.scope: Share of watercraft-related unintentional drowning deaths in the Royal Life Saving Society - Australia national drowning database, Australia, 2007-2011 (216 cases with activity 'watercraft', all ages, recreational and other; commercial fishing not separated) whose underlying cause of death was coded ICD-10 W65-W74: 63 (29%). Of all 1,428 unintentional drownings, 866 (60.6%) had W65-74 as underlying cause, 78 had V90 (5.5%) and 50 had V92 (3.5%). Not fisher-specific.
rows.source: Peden et al. (2017), Using a retrospective cross-sectional study to analyse unintentional fatal drowning in Australia: ICD-10 coding-based methodologies verses actual deaths, BMJ Open vol. 7, Table 2 (activity rows), Table 1 (V90, V92), Abstract, Discussion 'Water-related transport'
rows.do_not_add_to: An Australian coding share for all watercraft drownings, not fishers: do not apply it to any fisher count (fishing-ilo-1999, fishing-fao-32000, fishing-fsf-100000, the NIOSH or CFOI rows) to estimate an overlap, and do not combine with australia-2024-25 or other RLSSA annual counts (other years and case definitions). The 63 and 216 are not added to any count.
rows.note: The paper's point is that W65-W74 alone misses most watercraft drownings, consistent with ICD-10 placing drowning involving watercraft in V90 and V92. Other Table 2 rows: 'Rock fishing' 56 cases, 49 with W65-74; 'Non-aquatic transport' 115 cases, 15 with W65-74. Table 2 does not give V90/V92 counts by activity.

notes: Country tested: United States, through NIOSH's Commercial Fishing Incident Database (CFID) and the BLS Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries (CFOI). Result: partial. What is published: counts by the source's own incident types (vessel disaster, fall overboard, onboard, onshore, diving) for five-year periods, and 'drowning' as the reported cause of death (86% of 504 deaths in 2000-2009; 139 of 188, 75%, in 2010-2014). CFID codes every cause of death in ICD-10 from death certificates or investigative reports (Lincoln and Lucas 2010, Methods; MMWR 2010, Methods; Lucas and Case 2018, Case Definition), but no NIOSH document read prints the codes, so the fraction of fisher deaths inside W65-W74 cannot be stated for any year: the denominators exist (57 Alaska 2015-2019; 188 US 2010-2014; 24 CFOI 2024) but the numerator (deaths with underlying cause W65-W74) is unpublished. No single-year CFID count was found; NIOSH publishes periods. The missing step, exactly: a tabulation of CFID underlying-cause ICD-10 codes by incident type (held by NIOSH, Western States Division, Alaska) or an equivalent NOMS query. Reading the incident types against the ICD-10 rule (drowning after an accident to the watercraft = V90; drowning on board or overboard without accident to the watercraft = V92; W65-W74 only when no watercraft is involved), the Alaska 2015-2019 deaths explicitly described as drownings not involving a vessel are the 7 dock falls and 2 diving deaths; the 12 falls overboard and 21 vessel-disaster deaths would fall in V92/V90 if coded by the rule. That is a reading of categories, not a coded count, and the Australian evidence (Peden et al. 2017: only 63 of 216 watercraft drownings carried W65-74 as underlying cause, 29%) shows coding practice does not follow the rule exactly, so no fisher share was estimated. ICD-10 code titles were taken from Table 1 of Peden et al.; the icd-definition row already excludes V90/V92. Two other countries were opened but not made rows: Norway (Maritime Authority 2025 report lists fishing-vessel fatalities individually with events but no cause of death and no printed fishing total) and Japan (fiscal 2020 vital statistics by industry give, as extracted by the fetch tool, fishing-industry deaths 1,091 men and 330 women, of which accidents 96 men and 14 women; the drowning line is only in e-Stat tables). All figures were read through the fetch tool's text extraction of PDFs and pages, not from rendered pages; the reviewer should check by eye Figure 2 of NIOSH 2025-112 (labels 17, 12, 14, 7, 3, 4 against the text's 21/14/12/7/3), Table 2 of Peden et al. 2017 (216 and 63), and the Japanese figures. The Peden quote is printed with 'watercraft-related' broken across a line in the PDF. Author surnames are cited in the ledger's existing style; no other personal data recorded. The correction proposed for fishing-fsf-100000 only tightens its do_not_add_to rule; fishing-ilo-1999 already requires an overlap assumption and was left as is. Independent verification, 21 Oct 2026: every figure confirmed as printed; a reviewer should still confirm Figure 2 of NIOSH 2025-112 by eye (extracted labels 17, 12, 14, 7, 3, 4 against the text's 21/14/12/7/3).
